main_body: Japanese shrine hall: a large green tile roof slope over a cream shoji/red-post front wall with a dark lattice door, on a grey stone plinth
top_band: Green roof slope, rows 4-42 at x=48 (L 168 down to 47). It is a tall tiled surface with a ridge cap at rows 3-9, and it ends in a light tile edge at rows 42-43, just above the red beam.
evidence: The roof reads as a large sloped top surface, drawn like the reference house roofs. The tile rows darken toward the eave (L 66 then 47 at x=71), and a light tile edge plus a red beam at rows 44-46 mark the front edge. The wall below (rows 47-73) is a distinct vertical face with posts, and the dark lattice door sits inset between them. The stone plinth adds a base. Both major parts, roof and wall, are drawn as a roof over a front wall in the same way as the references, so the projection is three_quarter.

style.evidence: The roof tiles carry about 5 green steps with per-tile highlights, which is decent. The measured facts are weak, though. The piece has only 32 distinct colours against 66 and 185 for the references. Its median of 11 colours per tile only matches the simpler stone reference, not the richer one at 18. 83% of its dark edge pixels are neutral (the roof sides use #231d28), against 7-9% for the references, so the outline is a near-black sticker line rather than a dark tone of the adjacent material. The cream wall panels are large and mostly flat, with only sparse speckle. Beside the references it looks flatter and more sticker-like.
